title: Keep custom Windows Forms rendering aligned with Windows preferences
goal: Build a custom status control that reacts to renderer and Windows preference changes while retaining the owner contrast palette.

runtime.reason: Actual .NET 11 RC2 execution, not GA verification.
runtime.name: .NET

language.reason: Explicit sample language mode; .NET 10 comparison uses C# 14. No experimental language feature.
language.name: C#

packageAssets: Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App framework assets; no additional NuGet dependency. net10.0-windows comparison and net11.0-windows current sample.
providers: Local Windows desktop; no account or remote service
renderingModes: Native Windows Forms desktop; no Blazor render mode. See the recipe for renderer and reveal selection.
prerequisites: Use an STA thread and the declared exact SDK; available Windows Desktop reference packs are required.
constraints: Recorded .NET11 RC2 and .NET10 comparison only; no GA or other-platform behavior claim.
optIns: STA entry point and Windows Desktop runtime. No experimental API diagnostic suppression is required.
stabilityLimitations: Actual .NET11 RC2 evidence; GA reconciliation remains open.

selectionNotes: Previous release remains a comparison, not an additional .NET10 foundation.

evidence.scope: Real .NET10 previous-release compilation and shown-window lifecycle, using existing APIs only. No newer API/backport claim.
Real control handle, renderer selection, inherited requested mode and paint. Owner settings transitions are recorded separately as execution evidence.

PIN-897: owner-reported visual check and actual AccentColor/HighContrast notifications with Net11 -> Classic -> Net11, restoring High Contrast to its initial disabled state. No automated pixel, broad accessibility or GA verification.

humanProof.scope: PIN-897 owner check refreshed for SDK/runtime RC3 on 5 November 2026 in samples/net11.0/FenStatus/owner-settings.evidence.json. Pingu confirmed readable system-colour text with the decorative accent hidden in high contrast. Actual log shows initial disabled -> enabled/Classic -> restored disabled/Net11. Owner-reported readability; no broad accessibility or GA claim.
